title: Storage Limitation Principle
content: Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for no longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the personal data are processed. Organizations must define explicit retention periods or criteria used to determine that period.

title: Lawfulness of Processing & Legal Basis
content: Processing of personal data is lawful only if at least one legal basis applies: explicit consent, contractual necessity, compliance with legal obligations, protection of vital interests, performance of a public task, or legitimate interests pursued by the controller.

title: Data Subject Rights (Access, Rectification, Erasure)
content: Data subjects possess the right to obtain transparent confirmation and copies of their processed personal data (Art 15), rectify inaccurate data (Art 16), and request erasure without undue delay ('Right to be Forgotten' under Art 17) upon withdrawal of consent or termination.

title: Mandatory Data Processing Agreement (DPA) Terms
content: Processing by a processor shall be governed by a binding contract stipulating: processing solely on documented controller instructions, duty of confidentiality, implementation of Article 32 security measures, sub-processor engagement approval, assisting with data subject rights and breach notifications, deletion or return of data at contract termination, and submission to audits.

title: Security of Processing & Technical Safeguards
content: Controllers and processors must implement appropriate technical and organizational measures (TOMs), including encryption and pseudonymisation of personal data, continuous confidentiality and system resilience, ability to restore availability after an incident, and regular evaluation of security effectiveness.

title: Personal Data Breach Notification Timeline
content: In the event of a personal data breach, the controller must notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it. If the breach poses a high risk to data subjects, they must be notified without undue delay.

title: Cross-Border International Data Transfers
content: Transfers of personal data outside the EEA or UK require adequate protection safeguards, such as European Commission Adequacy Decisions, standard contractual clauses (SCCs) adopted by the Commission, Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs), or explicit statutory derogations.

title: Logical Access Control & Multi-Factor Authentication
content: The entity restricts logical access to confidential information and infrastructure through unique user accounts, role-based access control (RBAC), multi-factor authentication (MFA) for administrative and remote access, and prompt revocation of credentials upon employee or vendor termination.

title: Boundary Protection & Cryptographic Encryption Standards
content: The entity protects its perimeter through firewalls, network segmentation, intrusion detection systems, and encrypts confidential data both in transit over open/public networks (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or robust industry-standard encryption algorithms).

title: Security Incident Detection, Response & Escalation
content: The entity maintains documented incident response procedures to identify, analyze, contain, and escalate suspected security events, anomaly alerts, and unauthorized system access, including post-incident root cause review and stakeholder communications.

title: Change Management & Software Release Governance
content: The entity authorizes, designs, tests, approves, and documents configuration changes and software releases in staging environments prior to production deployment, preventing unreviewed code execution and maintaining rollback capabilities.

title: System Availability, Backups & Disaster Recovery
content: The entity performs scheduled, automated database and snapshot backups, verifies backup integrity through routine restoration testing, and establishes Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) to sustain business continuity during outages.

title: Privacy, Collection Notice & Data Sanitization
content: The entity provides explicit privacy notices detailing personal information handling, limits collection to authorized purposes, and securely disposes of, de-identifies, or destroys personal data once retention obligations expire.

title: Notice at Collection & Retention Disclosure
content: A business must provide a clear Notice at Collection disclosing the categories of personal information collected, the business purposes, and the explicit retention period (or criteria used) for each category. Data cannot be retained longer than reasonably necessary.

title: Consumer Rights: Right to Delete & Right to Know
content: Consumers have the right to request deletion of personal information collected from them, and the right to know categories and specific pieces of personal information collected, sources, and commercial purposes. Businesses must instruct service providers to cascade deletion requests.

title: Right to Opt-Out of Sale & Sharing (Do Not Sell/Share)
content: Consumers have the right to direct a business that sells or shares personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising not to sell or share it. The business must provide a conspicuous 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link and recognize Global Privacy Control (GPC) opt-out signals.

title: Service Provider Contractual Requirements & Prohibitions
content: Contracts with service providers must expressly prohibit: selling or sharing personal information, retaining, using, or disclosing personal information for any purpose other than the direct business purposes specified in the contract, and combining personal information received with data from other sources.

title: Limiting Use of Sensitive Personal Information
content: Consumers have the right to direct a business to limit the use and disclosure of sensitive personal information (such as government IDs, financial credentials, precise geolocation, biometric data) to what is strictly necessary to perform the requested services.

title: PIMS Context, Scope & Privacy Governance
content: The organization must determine its role as a PII controller and/or PII processor, document the scope of its Privacy Information Management System (PIMS), designate dedicated privacy roles, and establish information security policies approved by executive management.

title: PII Retention & Disposal Policies
content: PII shall not be retained for longer than is necessary for the purposes for which the PII is processed. Documented disposal procedures must be implemented, including secure erasure, cryptographic wipe, or physical destruction of media containing PII once the retention period ends.

title: Pre-contractual Privacy Alignment & Controller Duties
content: Prior to entering into contract commitments, organizations must verify compliance obligations, document customer responsibilities, and ensure contractual terms accurately describe the nature, purpose, categories of PII, and security controls.

title: Temporary File Sanitization & Purging
content: Procedures must be established to ensure that temporary files created during PII processing, batch operations, or system backups are systematically deleted or overwritten within defined timeframes in accordance with retention schedules.

title: PII Transmission Controls & Cryptography
content: PII transmitted over public communications networks or stored on portable media must be protected with strong cryptographic protocols to prevent unauthorized interception, tampering, disclosure, or data loss.

title: Consent Management & Privacy Incident Escalation
content: Mechanisms must be maintained to record valid consent, handle consent revocation, and respond to PII security breaches, including prompt notification to affected customers or controllers with relevant details to enable breach remediation.

title: Subcontractor Due Diligence & Processor Responsibilities
content: When engaging third-party subcontractors or cloud processors, the organization must perform security due diligence, enforce contractual flow-down clauses meeting PIMS requirements, and conduct regular audits of subcontractor compliance.
